Hey, I am interested in working upon this issue, can you please guide me on what exactly needs to be done, I have identified the portion you are talking about: 

https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/f22231de203450128dbfcd3277799d759d861abd/lib/ansible/plugins/connection/ssh.py#L320-L337

review_comments: @Akasurde this line was previously fully covered but now the branch coverage is partial. This means that the tests don't cover the else-branch of `if ssh_transfer_method is None`. Could you look into restoring coverage for this case?

This [PR](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/82902) fixes the default value so `get_option` would always set `ssh_transfer_method` to `smart` (default). I will remove this `if` block once https://github.com/ansible/ansible/pull/82902 is merged.

Not sure how well this test works since the removed option doesn't cause an error, but https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/devel/test/integration/targets/connection_ssh/runme.sh#L69 should use `ANSIBLE_SSH_TRANSFER_METHOD=scp` now.

```
        description:
            - "Preferred method to use when transferring files over ssh"
        choices: 
              sftp: This is the most reliable way to copy things with SSH.
              scp: Deprecated in newer OpenSSH, kept for backwards compatibility.  For OpenSSH >=9.0 you must add an additional option to enable scp (scp_extra_args="-O").
              piped: Creates an SSH pipe with C(dd) on either side to copy the data.
              smart: Tries each method in order (sftp > scp > piped), until one succeeds or they all fail.
         default: smart
```

@Akasurde this line was previously fully covered but now the branch coverage is partial. This means that the tests don't cover the branch when the body of the for-loop is skipped, when `methods == []`, for example. Could you look into restoring coverage for this case?
Additionally, on line 1307/1272 the else-branch (`methods == []`) is not covered anymore either.
Consequently, line 1312/1277 through the end of the method are not covered at all (due to tests always hitting a early `return`).
Finally, 1388/1353 now only has partial coverage (the tests only hit the else-branch, never raising the exception).
